verses.1: And he went forth through the gate of the valley. He came out from that gate to call upon us. He and all his people went forth to fight.
verses.2: And the LORD said to me, “Do not be afraid of him. For I have given him into your hands. With you are all his people and their land. You will do to him what you did to Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled in Hesbon.”
verses.3: And Jehovah our God gave us in our hands also the kingdom of the Babylonians, along with all their people. We conquered them until not a single survivor was left.
verses.4: And he conquered all those cities at that time. There was no “Kriya” among them; we didn’t take any of their cities from them. The king Og had sixty cities, each with its own walls.
verses.5: All these cities are located in difficult and high places, with high walls and gates. They are also far away from the cities of the periphery.
verses.6: And they were punished, just as we had done to King Heshbon. All the women and girls in those cities were killed.
verses.7: And all the animals and livestock in those cities became our prey.
verses.8: And at that time, that land was taken from two Amorite kings. They lived beyond the Jordan, from the river Arnon to Mount Hermon.
verses.9: The hunters will call him Sheriyon; the Amorites will call him Shninir.
verses.10: All the cities of the Mishor, and all the Gilad, and all the Bashan, right up to Salkha. And Edrei is also one of the cities of the Queen Og in Bashan.
verses.11: For only the king of the Babylonians remained among the doctors. His tomb is made of iron. It’s very large in size; it’s about six meters long and four meters wide.
verses.12: And this land was given to us at that time from the territory located on the banks of the Arnon River, as well as half of Mount Gilad. Its cities were given to my ancestors and to Gad.
verses.13: And the rest of the skin and all the flesh will be under my rule. I have given them to the half of the man. All the ropes that bind the flesh will be called “land of healing”.
verses.14: Yair ben Menashe took all the ropes that were used to bind the prisoners, right up to the borders of Geshuri and Ma’akhati. He named them after his own name: Chavt Yair. This is how it has been since that day.
verses.15: And to the one who knows, I have given the Gilead.
verses.16: And to my ancestors and descendants, I have given land from Gilad all the way to the stream Arnon. Along the banks of the stream, there is also land belonging to the people of Amun.
verses.17: And the Arabah, and the Yarden, and the region from Kinnereth to the sea of Arabah. The salty sea lies beneath the cliffs of Pisgah.
verses.18: And I command you at that time to say, “The LORD your God has given you this land to possess. You shall go before your brothers, the children of Israel, and all the descendants of Jacob.”
verses.19: I only know that from your birth, your upbringing, and your lineage. I know that a great amount of wealth will be placed in your hands, as I have given you that wealth.
verses.20: Until the Lord gives your brothers to you, so that they too may inherit the land that the Lord, your God, has given them across the Jordan. Then each person may go and inherit his own portion of the land that I have given you.
verses.21: And I commanded Joshua at that time to say, “Your eyes shall see all that Jehovah your God has done for these two kings. In the same way, Jehovah will do to all the kings you will defeat.”
verses.22: Do not be afraid, for the LORD your God is the one who will fight for you.
verses.23: And I prayed to the LORD at that time, with these words:
verses.24: O Adonai Yahweh, you have shown your power and greatness. You are the one who can do what you say. Your hands are strong; no one else has such power in heaven or on earth. You will do as you command.
verses.25: Please let me go over and see that good land. That land beyond the Jordan, that beautiful mountain, and all those fields of wheat.
verses.26: And Jehovah revealed His anger to you. But you did not listen to Me. Jehovah said to me, “My dear friend, do not repeat these words again.”
verses.27: Lift your head up, and look around with your eyes. Look from east to west. See for yourself that you cannot cross this Jordan River.
verses.28: And he commanded Joshua to strengthen him and to encourage him, so that he could go before this people. He would also give them the land that they would see.
verses.29: And he sat in the garden opposite the house of Peor.
